Article Title: 'Head of family PM Modi listens': BJP's Raghav Chadha hails 'historic' anti-paper leak Bill
Article Text:
BJP MP Raghav Chadha (ANI photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think stricter anti-paper leak laws will improve exam fairness? Yes, they will help No, more changes are needed 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: AAP turncoat and BJP MP Raghav Chadha on Thursday broke his prolonged silence on the paper leak issue, speaking for the first time from the ruling side in Rajya Sabha. As BJP pushed the anti-paper leak Bill in the Parliament, Chadha said he did not want headlines but spoke "wholeheartedly in support of the students of India," adding that "PM Modi heard it just like the head of a family listens. "Chadha stressed that the paper leak crisis could only be resolved through an "institutional solution" and not through "media sound-bytes", which he claimed was the approach adopted by the PM Modi-led government.BJP leader said, "I don't want headline, but an outcome."Addressing NEET aspirants, he said, "Your anger is justified. Your pain is real. And your concerns about the examination system are genuine."He further said that when students raised their voices in protest, the Prime Minister listened and acted as a "guardian" to address their concerns."Students demanded, the government acted. Historic decisions taken. System changed," Chadha said.He also said that the government "heard and delivered."Highlighting the impact of paper leaks on students, he added, "Because a paper leak does not merely compromise an examination. It can wipe out years of preparation in a single moment."He further said, "Every student deserves an examination system where hard work and merit, not a leaked paper, decide the result."Months ago, Chadha led a rebel exodus from Arvind Kejriwal-founded AAP, with seven Rajya Sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling BJP.However, the Bill came under sharp criticism from the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge led the attack after Union minister Jitendra Singh tabled the Bill in the Upper House.Parliament Thursday approved the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introducing stricter penalties for paper leaks and exam-related malpractices. The government said the legislation addresses one of the biggest concerns affecting students and called for cooperation from all stakeholders to tackle the issue.The Bill was passed by a voice vote in the Rajya Sabha amid an opposition walkout, a day after it cleared the Lok Sabha.Under the amended law, individuals found guilty of paper leaks or other unfair means in public examinations will face a minimum prison term of five years, extendable to 10 years, along with a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh.For organised exam-related crimes, the Bill prescribes a minimum jail term of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore.The legislation also empowers state governments and Union Territory administrations to designate Courts of Session as special fast-track courts to try offences under the Act. These courts will conduct day-to-day proceedings and complete trials within three months of the filing of the chargesheet.The Bill further authorises the central government to constitute a special task force to investigate offences under the Act whenever necessary.
Article Summary: BJP leader said, "I don't want headline, but an outcome" Chadha led a rebel exodus from Arvind Kejriwal-founded AAP, with seven Rajya Sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling BJP.

Article Title: ‘Unlucky’ taunts, dowry demands: Dehradun teacher dies, husband, in-laws booked
Article Text: DEHRADUN: A case has been registered against a personal secretary at the Uttarakhand Secretariat and his family members for allegedly causing the dowry death of his 27-year-old wife, Shristi Bhandari, a government school teacher, in Dehradun's Doiwala area.Acting on a complaint filed by the victim's mother, Seema Bhandari, police on Thursday registered an FIR under Section 80(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with dowry death, against Shristi's husband, Saurabh Khatri, his mother Parvina Devi, sister Charu Khatri and other unidentified family members.According to the complaint, Shristi married Khatri in November last year and lived with his family in Doiwala, around 20 km from Dehradun. Soon after the marriage, her husband and in-laws allegedly began subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty while demanding dowry.Circle Officer (Doiwala) Vandana Verma said the family regularly humiliated Shristi by calling her "inauspicious" and "unlucky"."They socially humiliated her, claiming that misfortunes began after her arrival. When her father-in-law passed away after a prolonged illness, the family blamed her for his death as well," CO Verma said.The incident came to light after Seema Bhandari was unable to contact her daughter on July 28 and 29 and asked relatives living nearby to check on her. They found Shristi in a critical condition at a local hospital. By the time her mother reached Dehradun from Srinagar in Garhwal, Shristi had died during treatment.
Article Summary: Shristi Bhandari, 27, a government school teacher, died in Dehradun's Doiwala area. Her husband and in-laws allegedly began subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty while demanding dowry. The family regularly humiliated Shristi by calling her "inauspicious" and "unlucky"

Article Title: Why’s CJI not on panel to pick CEC, Supreme Court asks government
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India

People must trust PM’s decisions, says SG Mehta amid challenge to authority

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Underscoring the need for an independent and impartial process for selection of the chief election commissioner and election commissioners, Supreme Court on Thursday said Election Commission must not only act independently but must also be seen to act independently. The court questioned why Parliament, while framing the law, decided not to include Chief Justice of India in the selection panel.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma said the CJI was part of selection panels for CBI director and Lokpal, and asked what could be the reason for excluding him from the process of selecting CEC and ECs — posts that are among the most important for a democracy. The court reserved its verdict on the Centre’s plea that the matter be referred to a constitution bench.The court is hearing challenges to the constitutional validity of the 2023 Act, under which CEC and ECs are appointed by President on the recommendation of a selection committee consisting of PM, leader of the opposition, and a Union Cabinet minister nominated by PM. SG Tushar Mehta argued that the court could not begin with an assumption that the PM would act against democratic principles.In 2023, a five-judge constitution bench of SC had directed that pending enactment of a law by Parliament, appointments should be made by a panel comprising the PM, CJI and leader of the opposition to infuse independence into the process. Parliament subsequently enacted the 2023 Act, which replaced the CJI with a cabinet minister.Attorney general (AG) R Venkataramani and solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta urged the bench not to question the wisdom of Parliament, arguing that doing so would amount to interference with the independence of the legislature. The AG said Parliament’s legislative choice could not be questioned merely because another model was possible, and that “Parliament cannot be gagged”. The SG added that the three organs of the state — executive, legislature and judiciary — were independent, and their independence must be respected.“People must trust the Prime Minister. The office of the Prime Minister has a sanctity attached… If his decision is not to be trusted and is to be seen as necessarily a bad-faith exercise, then why not have a provision that even while selecting his cabinet he must consult some former judge or outsider?” SG Mehta said.Mehta added that one organ of the state could not proceed on the basis that the PM and other ministers would act in bad faith or against constitutional principles simply because they have the numerical majority.The bench clarified that there was no question of not trusting the PM. However, it asked the SG how many ministers in the government had cases pending against them, recalling that the court had earlier reposed trust in the elected government to ensure that people with criminal antecedents were not appointed as ministers.“It is not a lack of faith. The election commissioner has to be an independent person. Should there not be a show of fairness? We are not saying fairness has not been achieved by this committee. Just like justice is not only to be done, it has to be shown to be done, we are on the second part,” the bench said.Government requested that the petitions be referred to a larger constitution bench, arguing that an important question of law was involved. This plea was strongly opposed by senior advocates D Seshadri Naidu, Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Prashant Bhushan and Sanjay Parikh, who contended that government was raising this ground after 20 days of hearing and should not be allowed to do so.In an affidavit, government countered the petitioners’ claim that the independence of Election Commission would be compromised by replacing CJI with a cabinet minister. It maintained that there was no flaw in the law passed by Parliament, and that free and fair elections had never been casualties even when appointments were made solely by the executive for over seven decades.Government described as hypothetical the suggestion that vesting the executive with exclusive authority in EC appointments would necessarily compromise the independence of the poll watchdog.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says Election Commission must not only act independently but must also be seen to act independently. Court questions why Parliament decided not to include Chief Justice of India in the selection panel. Court is hearing challenges to the constitutional validity of the 2023 Act.

Article Title: Supreme Court: No blanket ban on use of pellet guns for crowd control
Article Text:
File photo: Pellet gun use during jantar mantar protest

Both protesters and police human beings: Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed Delhi government to provide treatment to those injured during students’ protests but found a plea for ban on use of pellet guns for crowd control vague and asked when police are permitted to fire bullets in extreme situations, how could pellet guns be banned.Appearing for petitioners, advocate Vrinda Grover questioned the legality of Rapid Action Force using pellet guns against student protesters on July 20 at Jantar Mantar, and urged the SC to direct the Union govt to preserve the ammunition log of RAF during their deployment at the protest site and award exemplary compensation to those injured by metallic pellets.The petition was filed by Sheikh Irshad Mansoori and Prashant Kumar Singh, who suffered injuries from pellet guns on July 20, and former IPS officer Yashovardhan Azad.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed preservation of the logbook, and solicitor general Tushar Mehta said all documents required for an effective investigation into alleged police excesses and violence at the protest site would be preserved.When Grover persisted with the plea for a ban on use of pellet guns, Justice Bagchi termed the prayer vague and said, “Police regulations permit use of pellet guns in exceptional circumstances.If you want phasing out of pellet guns, then you must challenge those regulations, which you have not done.“You say at no stage metallic pellet can be used, when graded response permits use of bullets in extreme situations. Seeking ban on use of pellet guns cannot be on the same plane as seeking a ban on use of bullets (for crowd dispersal)? Law permits use of bullets.”Justice Bagchi recalled a Calcutta High Court order quashing a colonial-era police regulation asking personnel to fire at chests instead of legs of protesters to save ammunition.The bench said Azad needed to amend the relief sought in his petition as there could be an SOP for police’s graded action delineating when to use rubber pellets followed by metallic pellets. Grover agreed to amend the prayer to enable the SC to provide guidelines for the police’s crowd dispersal action.The bench reiterated that there were occasions when peaceful protests were hijacked by miscreants and became vehicles for ulterior purposes, including for the purpose of sabotaging the bona fide aim of the protests.“All such situations would require various graded responses. But most important is to equip police with adequate safety gear. Only then can they ponder over graded responses to violent crowds. Otherwise, the protesters and police, both are human beings and react equally to threats coming to them,” the bench said. The SG said citizens always have a right to non-violent protest.Grover said updated guidelines framed by Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPRD) were not available after 2016 and it was very difficult to obtain information from police. The bench said this was not correct and such guidelines should be uploaded on websites. The SG said he would check the veracity of Azad’s allegation.The SC had said on July 28 that it was prima facie convinced about a high-level inquiry into alleged police excesses and violence against cops and directed police to preserve data collected from various cameras but restrained them from taking coercive action against students and making public their personal data.Grover said petitioners Mansoori and Singh were injured by metallic pellets fired by RAF without provocation. She said while Mansoori received good treatment at Lady Hardinge Hospital, Singh did not, leading the SC to direct Delhi govt to provide adequate treatment to the two and all those injured during the protests led by CJP.
Article Summary: The petition was filed by Sheikh Irshad Mansoori and Prashant Kumar Singh, who suffered injuries from pellet guns on July 20. The bench said Azad needed to amend the relief sought in his petition as there could be an SOP for police’s graded action.

Article Title: 16 Indians, including 10 seamen, killed in Middle East conflict: Government

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi under fire: Anurag Thakur moves privilege notice over Lok Sabha speech
Article Text:
Rahul faces privilege notice: Anurag Thakur seeks action over 'unparliamentary' remarks

NEW DELHI: Union minister Anurag Thakur on Thursday moved a privilege motion against Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi , accusing him of using unparliamentary and derogatory expressions during the Monsoon Session and violating the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the house.In a notice submitted under Rules 222 and 223 of the Lok Sabha Rules, Thakur requested that the matter be admitted and referred to the Committee of Privileges for a detailed examination under Rule 227."Shri Rahul Gandhi has committed Breach of Privilege of member of Lok Sabha, Contempt of Lok Sabha and utter disregard to the authority of Hon'ble Speaker," the notice alleged.The move comes after Rahul Gandhi alleged that he was not allowed to speak during the debate on the anti-paper leak Bill and later repeated the claim at a press conference outside Parliament.In the privilege notice, Thakur alleged that Rahul Gandhi used expressions that were objected to by parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju during his speech in the Lok Sabha and continued using them despite objections and warnings from the Chair."Terming a section of citizens through such expressions on the floor of the House is offensive, derogatory, and demeans the dignity of Parliament, constituting contempt of the House," the notice stated.According to the notice, the remarks violated Rule 352 of the Rules of Procedure, which prohibits offensive and defamatory expressions, personal references questioning the bona fides of individuals, and remarks that demean any individual or class of persons.Thakur further alleged that Rahul Gandhi's conduct disrupted the functioning of the House and disregarded repeated directions from the Chair."He has conducted and behaved in the House in such a manner that it was obstructive in proper discharge of function of members of Lok Sabha individually and collectively as a House. He also did not follow the repeated instructions of the Hon'ble Speaker of the House," the notice said.The BJP leader alleged that Rahul Gandhi had committed a breach of privilege and contempt of the House and sought expunction of the disputed remarks from the official proceedings under Rules 380 and 381.The notice also requested that the matter be referred to the Committee of Privileges for a detailed inquiry and that Rahul Gandhi be directed to tender an unconditional apology to the House and the Union home minister.The development comes amid continuing political confrontation between the ruling BJP and the Opposition over the alleged NEET paper leak, police action against student protesters and repeated disruptions during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.
Article Summary: Union minister Anurag Thakur on Thursday moved a privilege motion against Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. The move comes after Rahul Gandhi alleged that he was not allowed to speak during the debate on the anti-paper leak Bill.

Article Title: Calling registered AYUSH doctors 'quacks' has no legal basis: NCISM
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a move likely to intensify the debate over the status of traditional medicine practitioners, the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) has warned that calling duly registered AYUSH doctors "quacks" or "bogus doctors" has no legal basis and could violate their legal and constitutional rights.The commission said it had come to its notice that qualified practitioners holding recognised degrees in Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa were being subjected to harassment, defamation and false characterisation through public notices, print and electronic media, social media platforms and other public forums.The NCISM said practitioners registered with the appropriate State Medical Councils for Indian Medicine and recognised under the Indian Medicine Central Council Act, 1970, and the NCISM Act, 2020, are legally recognised medical practitioners. It said the NCISM Act provides the statutory framework for regulating education, ethics and professional practice in Indian systems of medicine and confers legal rights and responsibilities on registered practitioners."There is no legal basis for describing such registered practitioners as 'quacks' or 'bogus doctors'," the commission said, adding that any individual, institution, media organisation or authority publicly using such terms may be acting contrary to the legal recognition granted under the NCISM Act, 2020, and may be infringing upon the practitioners' professional and constitutional rights.Reiterating its position, the commission said all duly qualified and registered practitioners of the Indian System of Medicine are legally recognised healthcare professionals and are entitled to the rights, protections and professional respect accorded to them under the law.The NCISM's stand is also consistent with the Centre's responses in Parliament, where the Ministry of AYUSH has repeatedly distinguished between unrecognised persons posing as AYUSH practitioners, who are liable for penal action under the law, and duly qualified and registered practitioners recognised under the NCISM Act.
Article Summary: The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine has warned that calling duly registered AYUSH doctors "quacks" or "bogus doctors" has no legal basis. The commission said qualified practitioners holding recognised degrees in Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa were being subjected to harassment, defamation and false characterisation.

Article Title: 'Can pellet guns be used against peaceful protesters under any circumstances?' CJP slams SC
Article Text:
The CJP has maintained that the march was peaceful and that the police response was disproportionate.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Thursday sharply challenged the Supreme Court’s observations on the use of pellet guns during student protests. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das accused the court of failing to rigorously examine whether the police action against peaceful demonstrators on July 20 was justified.Responding to the hearing on petitions related to the Delhi protest crackdown, Das said the court’s position raised serious questions about the use of force against non-violent protesters and who authorised it.“The Supreme Court has stated that pellet guns may be used in exceptional circumstances. First, did the peaceful protesters actually create such exceptional circumstances on July 20th?... There was no situation that warranted the use of pellet guns.... The Supreme Court should have rigorously examined whether the circumstances truly justified an action that caused a person to lose their eyesight. The second point is: Can pellet guns be used against peaceful protesters under any circumstances?. .. Ultimately, the Home Minister was responsible for supervision and issuing orders... The Supreme Court, too, needs to give serious and strict consideration to these matters, rather than simply rubber-stamping or endorsing such measures,” Das said.His remarks came after the Supreme Court heard a petition challenging the Delhi Police’s use of pellet guns during the July 20 march from Jantar Mantar to Parliament, during which several protesters were injured, and some allegedly suffered permanent loss of eyesight.The CJP has maintained that the march was peaceful and that the police response was disproportionate.According to the party, police attempted to stop the procession through a lathi charge and the firing of pellet guns. Das sought to place responsibility squarely on the government rather than on procedural justifications for the use of force.“The opposition is doing its job. Its role is precisely to ask questions and hold the government accountable. I saw that a discussion was taking place in Parliament. There ought to be a discussion on who issued the orders on July 20th, and who will answer for the conduct of the police towards the protesters and the brutality inflicted upon them? Naturally, the Home Minister should provide an answer regarding this matter,” he said.The remarks came as the CJP has continued to question the handling of the July 20 protests in both political and legal forums. Earlier, Das had also criticised a separate Supreme Court interim order in a batch of PILs related to the protests, arguing that it could allow governments to continue investigations against protesters despite what he described as the Centre’s assurance that FIRs would be withdrawn.For the CJP, the debate has moved beyond crowd control and entered the realm of public accountability. The party insists that the central question is not simply whether pellet guns can be used in exceptional circumstances, but whether the events of July 20 ever met that threshold in the first place.
Article Summary: The CJP has maintained that the march was peaceful and that the police response was disproportionate. The party insists that the central question is not simply whether pellet guns can be used in exceptional circumstances, but whether the events of July 20 ever met that threshold in the first place.

NEW DELHI: Parliament witnessed another stormy day on Thursday as the government pushed ahead with key legislation while the opposition intensified its attack over the alleged NEET paper leak and police action against protesting students. The Lok Sabha passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which makes insulting the national song Vande Mataram a punishable offence, while heated exchanges continued in the Rajya Sabha.The opposition also staged protests inside and outside Parliament, demanding that Union home minister Amit Shah answer allegations of excessive force against student protesters. In the Rajya Sabha, leader of the opposition Mallikarjun Kharge called for Shah's resignation, prompting a sharp response from Leader of the House J P Nadda, who accused the opposition of repeatedly disrupting Parliament.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired a high-level meeting with senior ministers to review India's preparedness in view of the ongoing crisis in West Asia, with the government saying there was no shortage of fuel, fertilisers or other essential supplies.The Lok Sabha passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 by voice vote amid noisy scenes in the House. The legislation extends to Vande Mataram the same legal protection already available to the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana.Under the Bill, intentionally preventing the singing of Vande Mataram or disrupting a gathering where it is being sung will become a criminal offence. The punishment is up to three years' imprisonment, a fine, or both. Repeat offenders will face a minimum jail term of one year.Replying to the debate, Minister of State for Home Nityananda Rai accused the Congress of failing to give the national song the respect it deserved during its years in power. He said the Modi government was restoring its rightful place and ended his speech with chants of "Vande Mataram".The opposition opposed the legislation. DMK MP Kanimozhi called it a "Hindutva agenda" disguised as nationalism. She argued that making all six stanzas compulsory went against the spirit of secularism and federalism. BJP MP Sambit Patra hit back, saying previous governments had failed to honour the national song.Soon after the Bill was passed, sloganeering broke out and the Lok Sabha was adjourned for the day. It is the first Bill to clear both Houses during the ongoing Monsoon Session.In the Rajya Sabha, Congress president and Leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge launched a sharp attack on the government while speaking on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.Kharge demanded Amit Shah's resignation over the alleged use of force against students protesting the NEET paper leak. He questioned who authorised the use of lathis, tear gas and pellet guns and claimed more than 100 students were injured.He also criticised the proposed anti-paper leak law, saying harsher punishments alone would not solve the problem. Kharge argued that the government had failed to strengthen the examination system and accused it of ignoring similar suggestions made by the Opposition in 2024.The Congress leader demanded a fixed annual examination calendar, a National Youth Employment Strategy, filling vacant government posts and an independent probe into the police action against protesters. He also accused the Centre of undermining academic freedom and making ideological appointments in universities.Government defends anti-paper leak BillReplying to the debate, Union Minister Jitendra Singh said the amendment reflected the government's commitment to protecting students and ensuring zero tolerance towards paper leaks.The Bill proposes stricter punishments for those involved in examination fraud. The minimum jail term for using unfair means will increase from three years to five years, with a maximum of 10 years. The maximum fine will rise from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 50 lakh.For organised examination-related crimes, the minimum punishment will increase to seven years, with fines of up to Rs 10 crore. The Bill also provides for Special Fast Track Courts and a Special Task Force to investigate such offences.Congress and other INDIA bloc MPs staged a protest outside Parliament, accusing the government of using excessive force against students and raising allegations over the theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.The MPs carried a donation box as a symbolic protest and raised slogans demanding that Amit Shah answer questions in Parliament.Inside the Rajya Sabha, Opposition MPs demanded that the Home Minister make a statement on the alleged police action. Chairman C P Radhakrishnan rejected the demand and continued with House business.The Opposition continued shouting slogans before staging a walkout. Responding to the protest, Leader of the House J P Nadda accused Opposition parties of repeatedly disrupting proceedings since the Monsoon Session began. He said the government was prepared to discuss every issue but alleged that the Opposition kept "changing the goalposts".Amid the developments in Parliament, Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired a nearly two-hour meeting with senior ministers and top officials to assess India's preparedness in view of the conflict in West Asia.Home Minister Amit Shah, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, BJP president J P Nadda, National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and other senior officials attended the meeting.According to government sources, ministries briefed the Prime Minister on the steps taken so far. The government said there was no shortage of petrol, diesel, LPG or fertilisers, and assured that adequate urea stocks were available for upcoming crop seasons.A day after it was passed in Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha on Thursday passed the anti-paper leak amendment bill.Union MoS Jitendra Singh earlier on Wednesday introduced the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 (anti-paper leak law) in the Rajya Sabha, describing it as a reaffirmation of the government's commitment to protecting the interests of students and youth.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha passes Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026. Bill makes insulting the national song Vande Mataram a punishable offence. Opposition also staged protests inside and outside Parliament, demanding that Union home minister Amit Shah answer allegations of excessive force against student protesters.

Article Title: 'Criticise govt, don't denigrate India': Harish Salve on dissent and social media

NEW DELHI: Senior advocate Harish Salve on Wednesday said criticism aimed at "keep[ing] the government in control" is essential in a democracy, but urged people not to "denigrate India" in today's world of social media.Speaking about the turmoil in the Western world, particularly in Europe, the former solicitor general said that despite its internal challenges, the West remains united in resisting India's rise, which he said it still views as "a third-world country"."Trenchant criticisms within India of the government and its institutions is necessary to keep the government in control. But we should be very careful. Whatever we say, whatever we do in today's world of social media, do not denigrate India as a nation. Always remember, 'Sare Jahan Se Achcha Hindustan Humara'," Salve was quoted as saying by the news agency ANI.Speaking at the AK Sen Memorial Lecture and Photograph Unveiling Ceremony organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA), Salve said holding those in power accountable is necessary in a constitutional democracy."One thing, as someone who resides outside India, is that India today is looked at with a great sense of respect.The Western world is in turmoil as we see every day. Europe feels orphaned. US is making people wonder whether it ever had a Constitution. But they unite when it comes to resisting India's ascent. They still find it hard to accept that a country of not white people, a country which they call a third-world country, is aspiring to be a leader of the world, has become the fourth largest economy in the world," Salve was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.The event marked the unveiling of a portrait of late Senior Advocate and former Union law minister AK Sen in Library No. 1 of the Supreme Court. Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant joined Salve in unveiling the photograph.Several senior members of the legal fraternity attended the ceremony. SCBA President and Senior Advocate Vikas Singh paid tribute to Sen's contribution to the legal profession, while Attorney General for India R. Venkataramani also spoke about his legacy.Addressing the gathering, Chief Justice Surya Kant described Sen as a distinguished lawyer, scholar and statesman whose career reflected a lifelong commitment to justice and public service. He said the portrait would honour Sen's contribution while inspiring future generations of advocates."Today, we are not merely adorning our Library with a fitting tribute; we are enshrining in these walls the spirit of a life devoted to justice, intellect and public service... For every Advocate who passes through the Library, this portrait would be a silent reminder that our calling transcends personal ambition, that the practice of law and the stewardship of justice are sacred trusts in service of the Republic," the Chief Justice said.He added that the portrait should remind young lawyers of the values expected from members of the legal profession."A young lawyer rushing to Court with a first brief may pass this portrait. I hope the portrait will ask the more important questions that Mr Sen no doubt asked himself sometimes: Have I prepared enough? Have I been fair to the Court and to my opponent? Have I used the law to clarify, or merely to complicate?... May his presence here remind us that brilliance without balance is incomplete; that office without service is transient; and that law without humanity is barren," the Chief Justice said.
Article Summary: Senior advocate Harish Salve said criticism aimed at "keep[ing] the government in control" is essential in a democracy. Salve urged people not to "denigrate India" in today's world of social media. He said the West remains united in resisting India's rise, which he said it still views as "a third-world country"

Article Title: Spain migrant crisis: Military deployed as thousands cross border; 9 killed
Article Text:

Spain has announced the deployment of its military to Ceuta after thousands of migrants crossed into the North African enclave from Morocco, triggering, what the authorities and people are describing as one of the territory's worst border crises in years. At least nine people died during the mass crossings.The government said the Armed Forces would assist the Civil Guard to “maintain security in the city of Ceuta.”, while Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska travelled to Ceuta on Friday to oversee the response.The latest crisis unfolded on Thursday when thousands of migrants crossed into Ceuta by swimming around breakwaters, using inflatable devices or scaling the border fence. Videos showing large crowds celebrating as they entered Spanish territory quickly spread on social media, highlighting the scale of the influx.Officials said the sudden surge overwhelmed security forces. "The situation is absolute chaos," said Rachid Sbihi, head of the association representing Civil Guard officers in Ceuta, adding that the border had "totally collapsed", as quoted by AP.Spanish authorities did not provide an official figure for the number of arrivals, but state broadcaster TVE estimated that between 2,000 and 3,000 migrants entered Ceuta within hours.Ceuta President Juan Jesús Vivas said the territory had already been receiving around 300 migrants by sea each day in recent weeks, leaving reception centres overstretched even before Thursday's influx.Read more: Videos of Moroccan migrants entering Spain after swimming around border barriers go viral Vivas urged Madrid to declare a national emergency and deploy the military, warning that the autonomous city lacked the capacity to manage the crisis on its own.Spain later confirmed that it had reached an agreement with Morocco to facilitate the return of migrants who entered Ceuta illegally, although no timeline for the repatriations has been announced. Spain's Interior Ministry said Moroccan authorities were cooperating to prevent further crossings and stop people attempting to reach the enclave.Morocco's embassy in Madrid blamed criminal networks involved in migrant smuggling and human trafficking for the mass crossings, saying Moroccan authorities did not support or encourage the movements.The reason behind the sudden influx remains unclear. Some local authorities suggested a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling, which bars the immediate return of migrants arriving by sea without due process, may have encouraged more people to attempt the crossing. However, migrant rights activists questioned that explanation, arguing that most migrants were unlikely to have been aware of the court's decision.The latest emergency echoes the 2021 Ceuta border crisis, when more than 8,000 migrants entered the enclave in just two days after Morocco was accused of relaxing border controls during a diplomatic dispute with Spain.Ceuta, along with Melilla, is one of the European Union's only two land borders with Africa and has long been a focal point for irregular migration into Europe.
Article Summary: Thousands of migrants crossed into the North African enclave from Morocco. At least nine people died during the mass crossings. The Armed Forces will assist the Civil Guard to ‘maintain security in the city of Ceuta’ Spain's Interior Ministry said Moroccan authorities were cooperating to prevent further crossings.

Article Title: Nepal communal violence: Three killed, curfew widens; PM Balendra Shah appeals for calm
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view What is the best way to maintain peace during communal tensions? Dialogue and understanding Stronger security measures 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Nepal prime minister Balendra Shah on Thursday appealed for unity, restraint and social harmony after at least three people were killed in communal violence that began in Sunsari district and later spread to neighbouring Madhesh province. The violence prompted authorities to expand curfews and tighten security across several districts.Addressing the nation for the first time since the violence erupted, Shah said the government was treating the situation with its "full seriousness and sensitivity" and pledged a fair and transparent investigation into the clashes."The Government of Nepal is completely serious and sensitive about the tragic incident that took place in Dewanganj, Siraha and other places in Sunsari a few days ago and the turbulent atmosphere that has arisen in some districts since then," Shah said in the televised address.The government's response comes amid curfews, prohibitory orders and heightened security deployments in Sunsari, Siraha, Dhanusa and Parsa districts. Since Sunday, protests and tensions have spread across Nepal's southern plains, raising concerns over wider communal friction in areas bordering India.Violence spread to neighbouring Madhesh province on Thursday, where a teenager died during clashes in Golbazar market in Siraha district.Officials also confirmed that a person injured in the earlier violence in Sunsari succumbed to injuries in Koshi province, taking the death toll to three.According to officials, the unrest began late on Sunday in Ward No. 3 of Dewanganj rural municipality in Sunsari district after a dispute between local groups over loud music during preparations for the Bol Bam pilgrimage to the Saptakoshi River. AFPreported that tensions escalated over loud music and religious flags during a Hindu procession, prompting police to open fire to disperse the crowd, according to local official Poshan Lamichhane.The confrontation escalated into stone-pelting and violence, prompting police to intervene with batons, tear gas, warning shots and eventually live fire by the Armed Police Force. One person died on the spot from gunshot injuries, while several others were critically injured.Shah announced that the ministry of home affairs had formed an investigation committee and assured the public that those responsible would be prosecuted."As soon as the incident happened, all security agencies immediately reached the spot and made continuous efforts to normalise the situation, prevent further unpleasant incidents and maintain peace and security. The Ministry of Home Affairs has formed an investigation committee to conduct a fair investigation into the incident and take strict legal action against the culprits." he said.The prime minister said the government had adopted a multi-pronged approach to restore normalcy. He said an all-party meeting had been convened at the central level, while continuous dialogue was under way with local representatives, civil society members, religious leaders, community representatives and social activists."In addition, a meeting of the National Security Council has been convened to seriously review the overall peace and security situation in the country and necessary decisions have been taken according to the situation," Shah said.In his four-and-a-half-minute televised address, Shah also urged citizens not to circulate misinformation or inflammatory content that could worsen tensions." The essence of all religions is compassion, mercy, love and peace. Blaming an entire community for an unexpected and tragic incident in one part of the country and spreading the fire of revenge for it in other parts of the country cannot be justified or justified from any perspective," he said.Concluding his address in both Nepali and Maithili, Shah appealed for collective efforts to restore peace and preserve national unity."Our history is a witness that even in the most difficult and difficult situations, mutual unity, tolerance and conscience have become our greatest strength. We all have to play the role of responsible citizens and remove the clouds of unrest that have hung over this beautiful and peaceful Nepali sky. We, the common citizens, civil society, religious communities, all respected leaders, all political parties and responsible media, are making a heartfelt appeal to the government to exercise patience and restraint and maintain peace, harmony, brotherhood and national unity," he said.
Article Summary: Nepal's prime minister Balendra Shah appeals for unity, restraint and social harmony. Shah says the government is treating the situation with its "full seriousness and sensitivity" The violence prompted authorities to expand curfews and tighten security across several districts.

Article Title: CJP protest in Mumbai: Cop ‘inappropriately touches’ woman in video, stirs row
Article Text:
The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage.





MUMBAI: A viral video from the CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Thursday, showing a policeman allegedly inappropriately touching a woman protester, stirred up a fresh controversy on Friday, with the opposition demanding his dismissal.The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage.DCP (operations) Akbar Pathan said, “The official was trying to hold on to a male protester and a lady stepped in while he was looking away. Senior officers have verified all the facts and minutely assessed the video to ascertain the facts,” he said.Another police official said, “Since the video went viral late Thursday night, our senior cyber crime experts carefully zoomed in on the footage, verified it, and found that there was no misconduct.”The controversy came a day after another viral video showed a police constable, who was working as a driver, allegedly threatening young protesters that drugs would be planted on them and their career would be ruined if they continued participating in protests.The latest video quickly went viral on social media, with several opposition politicians demanding action against the policeman. Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded an apology from CM Devendra Fadnavis and dismissal of the policeman.In a post on X, Sapkal said, “The one who calls himself Devabhaau has turned out to be Duryodhan! Devabhaau’s police have become so rogue that they are violating the modesty of female students the age of their own daughters.”Mumbai Congress president and MP Varsha Gaikwad said, “What happened to a girl during the protest in Mumbai is deeply painful and disturbing. It is wrong to speak of the ‘Ladki Bahin’ scheme while treating young women in such a manner. It is a matter of shame that women are allegedly being mistreated in the land of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. False cases are being registered against students, and they are being threatened. ”Congress has organised statewide candlelight marches and ‘satyagraha’ in Maharashtra on Saturday to express solidarity with the protesting students.
Article Summary: The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage. The controversy came a day after another viral video showed a police constable, who was working as a driver, allegedly threatening young protesters.

Article Title: 3 years on, SIT probe complete in just 10% of Manipur riot cases
Article Text: NEW DELHI: More than three years after Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives, Supreme Court was informed Friday that probes into only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by SITs of state police while CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.Appearing for the CBI, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the central probe agency had filed chargesheets in 21 cases and closure reports in six, of which three had been accepted. It was continuing investigations into the remaining four cases.Former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar, who was appointed to oversee the investigations, informed the court through a report that of the 3,020 cases being probed by the SITs across eight districts, chargesheets had been filed in only 301 cases and trial had commenced in 10.The CJI-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously. Given the volume of cases, SC mulled setting up special courts to try these exclusively. It sought responses to this from Manipur govt and the high courts of Assam and Manipur.SC had transferred investigations into cases of rape-murder other heinous offence to CBI and shifted their trial to Guwahati. The central agency told the court that examination of witnesses residing in Manipur through video-conferencing was a challenge because of law-and-order situations, non-cooperation and language barriers as they spoke different dialects.Senior advocate Ngangom Junior Luwang complained that no effort had been made to trace 30 missing people and without their remains, authorities were not issuing death certificates required for other purposes. SC asked him to approach Manipur high court.Advocate Sharukh Alam submitted that land belonging to churches vandalised during the clashes were getting encroached upon and said govt had taken no steps to reconstruct them. Bhati said govt's priority was to reconstruct damaged dwelling units. The bench said govt was right to prioritise reconstructing houses but asked it to take steps to stop encroachment of places of worship.
Article Summary: Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives. Only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by state police. CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.

Article Title: 'Ab aayega aur maza!' CJP says 'time is ticking' as farmers announce march to Jantar Mantar on Sunday
